subject: Workplace Skills
title: Building Consensus Before the Vote
description: A short lesson to help you apply Building Consensus Before the Vote.

hook.text: A product director met individually with each stakeholder before the planning meeting. Her proposal passed easily.

buildup.text: Springing proposals on people in meetings triggers defensiveness. Pre-alignment eliminates surprise resistance.

discovery.text: One-on-one conversations before a group decision let you hear concerns privately and adjust your approach.

twist.text: Pre-alignment is not cheating. It's inclusive. It gives introverts and skeptics a safe space to contribute.

climax.text: Before any big proposal, brief each key stakeholder individually. Address their concerns before the room hears them.

punchline.text: Build agreement one person at a time. Meetings just confirm it.

quiz.question: Why is pre-aligning with stakeholders before a group decision effective?
options: It eliminates the need for any formal meeting
It lets you hear concerns privately and reduces surprise resistance
It ensures only your supporters attend the meeting
